questions.question: The finance team must receive an email when the actual monthly cost of a subscription reaches 80 percent of 5,000 USD. What should you create?

options.text: A budget of 5,000 with an Actual alert condition at 80 percent and the finance team as recipients
options.why: Correct. Budgets send alerts when cost reaches thresholds.

options.text: An Azure Policy assignment that denies resources after 80 percent of spend
options.why: Azure Policy does not evaluate spend.

options.text: An Azure Advisor alert for cost recommendations
options.why: Advisor alerts notify about recommendations, not spending thresholds.

options.text: A metric alert on CPU percentage
options.why: Metric alerts monitor resource metrics, not cost.

questions.explanation: Budget alert conditions use Actual or Forecasted cost at a percentage of the budget amount.

questions.question: Virtual machines in a development subscription must be deallocated automatically when spending reaches 90 percent of the monthly budget. Which two components should you configure? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: A budget alert condition at 90 percent that uses an action group
options.why: Correct. The budget alert triggers the action group.

options.text: An action group that runs an Azure Automation runbook or a logic app to deallocate the VMs
options.why: Correct. Automation performs the deallocation.

options.text: A spending limit on the budget that stops resources
options.why: Budgets do not stop resources by themselves.

options.text: A ReadOnly lock on the subscription
options.why: A ReadOnly lock would also block the deallocation.

questions.explanation: Budgets only notify. Action groups connect alerts to automation.

questions.question: You need to be notified before month end if spending is projected to exceed the budget. Which alert type should you use?

options.text: Forecasted
options.why: Correct. Forecasted alerts fire when projected cost will reach the threshold.

options.text: Actual
options.why: Actual alerts fire only after cost has been accrued.

options.text: Anomaly
options.why: Anomaly alerts detect unusual daily spending patterns, not budget projections.

options.text: Service Health
options.why: Service Health alerts report Azure platform issues.

questions.explanation: Combine Actual alerts at lower thresholds with a Forecasted alert at 100 percent.

questions.question: You need to identify virtual machines that are underutilized so you can resize or shut them down. What should you use?

options.text: Azure Advisor cost recommendations
options.why: Correct. Advisor identifies low-utilization VMs and estimates savings.

options.text: Azure Policy compliance
options.why: Policy reports rule compliance, not utilization.

options.text: Access control (IAM) Check access
options.why: Check access shows permissions, not utilization.

options.text: Resource locks
options.why: Locks protect resources and provide no recommendations.

questions.explanation: Advisor recommends right-sizing or shutting down underutilized VMs, reservations and removing unused resources.

questions.question: Three departments share one subscription. Each department must have its own monthly budget. Resources are tagged with a department tag. What should you do?

options.text: Create three budgets at the subscription scope, each filtered on a different department tag value
options.why: Correct. Budget filters can scope spend by tag.

options.text: Create one budget and divide the amount by three
options.why: A single budget cannot alert each department separately.

options.text: Create three management groups under the subscription
options.why: Management groups cannot be created under a subscription.

options.text: Apply a CanNotDelete lock for each department
options.why: Locks do not track cost.

questions.explanation: Enforce the tag with Azure Policy so that the budget filters are accurate.
